headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared execution or filesystem surfaces, but Great Expectations can ingest files and LightZero is a local-only game agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. agent_a can read files for data sources and validation results, but agent_b has no filesystem read, MCP, browser, or subprocess surface, so there is no plausible default path for agent_a content to be parsed as instructions by agent_b.
conditions: IF a manual copy-paste or external bridge is introduced between the agents, prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no clipboard or message-queue bridge.
Do not pipe agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts.
Review any future orchestrator for shared channels before enabling them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches data quality tests, validation results, and documentation, but agent_b has no filesystem read, write, or network egress. With no shared workspace or outbound channel on agent_b, there is no documented path for agent_a data to leak through the pair by default.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is mounted and agent_b gains file-read access, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid mounting sensitive data into any shared directory.
Store validation artifacts in a separate workspace from any sensitive inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can install packages and work with files, but agent_b cannot write files, modify git state, execute shells, or spawn subprocesses. Because the write-capable surfaces do not overlap, there is no capability conflict in the default pair configuration.
conditions: IF agent_b is later granted filesystem or git write access to the same directory as agent_a, conflict risk appears.
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only or fully isolated.
Do not grant shared git or filesystem write permissions.
If writes are added, introduce locking or separate worktrees.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error pathway is weak because agent_b is a game-playing agent with no documented action-taking or file/network authority, so it is unlikely to operationalize agent_a's outputs. The main residual risk is manual misuse if an operator forwards agent_a's validation results into agent_b without review.
conditions: IF an operator copies agent_a outputs into agent_b as authoritative instructions, downstream mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing agent_a outputs.
Do not treat validation results as commands.
Keep agent_b disconnected from any automation pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is documented. agent_a touches documentation and validation results, while agent_b touches no data classes and has no network egress or storage surfaces, so there is no evidenced residency, retention, or regulated-data transfer issue in this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is later introduced into agent_a's files and agent_b gains access, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair unless a policy review is completed.
Document retention rules for validation artifacts.
Reassess if either agent gains external connectivity.
